correctness.rationale: The explicit XOR generators produce the five-regular 16-vertex graph with forty edges and strongly regular counts. The subset recurrence enumerates all 2^16 induced-edge counts and all 3^16=43,046,721 named three-color assignments, providing complete minima/counts for each of seventeen favored-population sectors; the independent base-3 code computes the same arrays from direct edges. All five knots are exact rationals; comparing every omitted line at each knot plus affine interpolation and tail slopes proves global envelope validity. The saturation count also equals the independently enumerated independence polynomial evaluated at two. Both package verifiers executed and agreed.

originality.rationale: The explicit seventeen-sector Clebsch three-color minimum/count table, five magnetic-field crossings and six-sector saturation degeneracy were not supplied by the examined relevant primary texts or published mathematical-record summaries. The general graph-polynomial formulas have arbitrary-graph scope but require a nontrivial Clebsch-specific coefficient computation and do not themselves state the evaluated field diagram. A same-graph Ising result concerns two states and cannot imply the three-state occupancy-sector counts. Historical priority remains provisional; unindexed exact Clebsch tables are a residual risk.
residual_risks: Some older exact Clebsch Potts or max-three-cut tables might be unindexed or reported in a book or unpublished computation; absence from searched sources is not proof of priority.
The equivalence of general magnetic Potts and graph-polynomial formulations is established prior art; the claim of novelty is only the specific evaluated five-threshold and 17-sector result.
The saturation independence-set identity is generic; only its role in the evaluated Clebsch field diagram is part of this result.

value.rationale: The five-regular Clebsch graph is the canonical unique (16,5,0,2) triangle-free four-chromatic strongly regular graph and folded 5-cube. Because three colors cannot properly color it, the exact minimum frustration count and the complete labeled field-response diagram are natural finite magnetic invariants. The five exact coexistence fields, all seventeen sector counts and the six-sector 4065-fold saturation boundary yield a nontrivial reproducible benchmark for frustrated Potts calculations. The precise object/invariant is motivated before counting; this is a complete finite classification, not a generic theorem or a thermodynamic assertion.
